text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Estonia welcomes Russia's intention to improve relations, Estonian Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves said about the remarks of Boris Yeltsin on Saturday about the Baltic security.
- Estonia and Japan should sign an agreement on avoiding double taxation, Estonian President Lennart Meri said at a meeting with the Japanese prime minister in Tokyo.
- A film by Estonian Mark Soosaar about the Khanti people in Siberia won the main Nanook award at the festival of etnographic films in Paris.
- Crews of ferries that navigate between the Estonian islands and the mainland demand a pay-rise.
- The volunter Defence League was forced to rent its buildings and offer guarding services because state funding was insufficient, chief Neeme Vali said.

- Former Soviet passports will not be accepted in paying pensions after May 15, their owners should acquire either the aliens passport or a passport issued by their home country, social ministry officials warn.
- A car registration centre will in future note the passing of the technical inspection in vehicle documents due to the forging of test pass cards.
- Tallinn city government chose the Union Bank to manage its accounts with an estimated turnover of two billion kroons a year.
